raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What & why

DeepSeek-V4-Flash can render an inline system message as bare content appended to the preceding user span. Its custom encoder uses `system_msg_template = "{content}"`, so a request such as `[user: Q, system: LATESYS, user: Q2]` becomes `<|User|>QLATESYS<|User|>Q2` rather than a structurally distinct system instruction.

A template rendering without an error is therefore not sufficient evidence that preserving an inline system message is safe. This PR uses a safe default: merge text system messages into one leading system message before rendering. The policy applies consistently to both OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages, including Anthropic token counting.

## Changes

- Add `--inline-system-messages {merge,preserve}`; `merge` is the default.
- Normalize system messages in `OpenAIServingChat` immediately before rendering, covering both OpenAI and Anthropic requests.
- Remove Anthropic-only template-error detection and endpoint-local message merging.
- Preserve remains available as explicit opt-in for deployments whose model/template behavior is independently validated and where prefix-cache stability is more important.
- Add regressions that show the DeepSeek-V4 renderer welded prompt under `preserve` and the corrected leading-system prompt under `merge`.
- Add an Anthropic conversion regression proving it uses the shared policy.

## Behavior

| Mode | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `merge` (default) | Merge text system messages into one leading system message before rendering. |
| `preserve` | Keep system messages at their original positions. Intended only for verified model/template combinations. |

## Verification

- `git diff --check`
- `.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q vllm/entrypoints/openai/cli_args.py vllm/entrypoints/generate/api_router.py vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`
- The focused pytest command could not run locally because the existing `.venv` does not contain `pytest`; CI remains required.

## Not a duplicate

This supersedes the Anthropic-only policy in the previous revision of this PR. Related PR #46196 concerns resolving a model template before an Anthropic-only auto-detection decision; this PR removes the unsafe render-success heuristic and normalizes the request once at the shared OpenAI rendering boundary.

Fixes #46710

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to prepare this patch. The submitter reviewed the changed lines.

Thanks for the credit, and nice work reworking this. The merge-by-default approach with explicit `preserve` opt-in matches what we saw on DeepSeek-V4-Flash: once the inline system text is welded into the preceding user span, successful rendering clearly isn't a meaningful safety check.

The shared handling across OpenAI and Anthropic is a much cleaner direction. We do have access to Kimi-K3 and can run the same `[user, system, user]` `/tokenize` check when that lane is back up. I'll post the render once we have it running again.

Rechecked this against current `main` and the newer related work. Head `3b4eb88daab61ce35526160e462c104e9882ddad` is currently mergeable; the latest `pre-commit` workflow is only failing the authorization pre-run gate, with the actual pre-commit job skipped. CodeRabbit and Read the Docs are green.

Two concrete things still look worth resolving before merge:

1. The structured-content case from @StevenConnors is still real on this head. `_normalize_inline_system_messages()` only selects system messages whose `content` is a `str`, so a list/block-form inline system message is left in place and can still reach a system-first template. The existing Anthropic `_extract_system_text()` path shows how to flatten text blocks without dropping them.

2. There is now an explicit policy conflict with #53501 and #56520. #56520 improves prefix-cache reuse by preserving DeepSeek inline system turns, but the regression in this PR demonstrates why renderability alone is not enough: DeepSeek can render `[user, system, user]` as user content with no distinct system-role marker. #53501 instead re-roles the inline system turn to `user`, which keeps the prompt append-only but intentionally changes role semantics.

Given that, I would avoid treating `supports_inline_system_messages` as equivalent to preserving system semantics. The current `merge` default + explicit `preserve` opt-in is the safer general contract unless maintainers prefer a third explicit policy (for example re-role-to-user / drop) to make the cache-vs-semantics tradeoff operator-controlled.

I don't think a new competing PR is useful here; #47681 is already the right place to settle the shared policy. Once the structured-content case and policy direction are agreed, the remaining mechanical work is small.

I prepared the structured-content fix separately so it can be cherry-picked without mixing it into the policy discussion: `Blackwellboy/vllm@7e947a6b212a68fc2bd55924ac15753fc4e760b4`.

It is based exactly on current head `3b4eb88` and only changes two files. The merge path now accepts list-form system content when every part is textual (`{"type":"text","text":...}`), merges those parts the same way as string content, and fails closed by leaving the request untouched if it encounters unsupported structured content rather than dropping anything.

The regression now mirrors the reported shape directly: a leading structured system message plus a later structured system message around user turns, rendered through DeepSeek V4. No policy behavior changes are included.

I changed the PR from Anthropic-only, template-error-based detection to a shared merge-by-default policy after the issue discussion showed that successful rendering does not prove a model preserves inline system-message boundaries. @bbrowning provided the core guidance to merge unless support is verified; @chaunceyjiang highlighted the prefix-cache tradeoff, motivating explicit preserve opt-in; @felix0080 supplied cross-model evidence; and @Blackwellboy plus @wqh17101 identified the concrete DeepSeek-V4-Flash failure: its encoder welds inline system text into the preceding user span. Two concrete things still look worth resolving before merge:

1. The structured-content case from @StevenConnors is still real on this head. `_normalize_inline_system_messages()` only selects system messages whose `content` is a `str`, so a list/block-form inline system message is left in place and can still reach a system-first template. The existing Anthropic `_extract_system_text()` path shows how to flatten text blocks without dropping them.

2. There is now an explicit policy conflict with #53501 and #56520. #56520 improves prefix-cache reuse by preserving DeepSeek inline system turns, but the regression in this PR demonstrates why renderability alone is not enough: DeepSeek can render `[user, system, user]` as user content with no distinct system-role marker. #53501 instead re-roles the inline system turn to `user`, which keeps the prompt append-only but intentionally changes role semantics.

Given that, I would avoid treating `supports_inline_system_messages` as equivalent to preserving system semantics. The current `merge` default + explicit `preserve` opt-in is the safer general contract unless maintainers prefer a third explicit policy (for example re-role-to-user / drop) to make the cache-vs-semantics tradeoff operator-controlled.

I don't think a new competing PR is useful here; #47681 is already the right place to settle the shared policy. Once the structured-content case and policy direction are agreed, the remaining mechanical work is small.

I prepared the structured-content fix separately so it can be cherry-picked without mixing it into the policy discussion: `Blackwellboy/vllm@7e947a6b212a68fc2bd55924ac15753fc4e760b4`.

It is based exactly on current head `3b4eb88` and only changes two files. The merge path now accepts list-form system content when every part is textual (`{"type":"text","text":...}`), merges those parts the same way as string content, and fails closed by leaving the request untouched if it encounters unsupported structured content rather than dropping anything.

The regression now mirrors the reported shape directly: a leading structured system message plus a later structured system message around user turns, rendered through DeepSeek V4. No policy behavior changes are included.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@chaunceyjiang @bbrowning Hi, following up on the discussion in #46710 — felix0080's tests confirmed the issue with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-PD, and this PR implements the approach discussed there. Could you kindly add the ready label to trigger CI when you have a moment? Thank you!

I changed the PR from Anthropic-only, template-error-based detection to a shared merge-by-default policy after the issue discussion showed that successful rendering does not prove a model preserves inline system-message boundaries. @bbrowning provided the core guidance to merge unless support is verified; @chaunceyjiang highlighted the prefix-cache tradeoff, motivating explicit preserve opt-in; @felix0080 supplied cross-model evidence; and @Blackwellboy plus @wqh17101 identified the concrete DeepSeek-V4-Flash failure: its encoder welds inline system text into the preceding user span. The updated approach protects both OpenAI and Anthropic paths while preserving an explicit option for validated deployments.
